newsitem.title: PANAMA: Greenpeace opposes nuclear shipment in Panama canal.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace opposes nuclear shipment in Panama canal.

text.p: The international environmental group Greenpeace asked Panama on Thursday to prevent a British-registered freighter carrying radioactive nuclear waste from Japan to Europe from using the Panama Canal.
"We'd like to see the government of Panama oppose this type of high-level nuclear waste shipments like other Caribbean nations have done," Greenpeace spokesman Tom Clements said.

He told a news conference the number of spent nuclear fuel shipments worldwide was about 200, "but there has only been one high-level nuclear waste shipment. If this goes through the Panama Canal, it would set a precedent for more types of shipments."

The vessel, scheduled to pass through the canal early next year, will carry nuclear waste in solid form to France from Japan, Clements said. The fuel was removed from reactors in Japan and would be sent to processing plants in France and Britain.

An official from British Nuclear Fuels, which organises the shipments, said company ships have been passing safely through the Panama Canal since the 1960s. He said the name of the vessel and the tonnage of the ship in question would not be released until the time of the voyage.
"There is nothing secretive about this shipment. We're carrying used fuels in compliance with United Nations regulations," Gavin Carter, international transport coordinator, told Reuters.
"The shipment will take place sometime early next year. We will announce the route in advance," he added.
